scope: R3-04 and R7-08/09 fixed video review, ordered recovery drafts and lost-receipt recovery
findings: Draft writes entered RecoveryStore only after asynchronous media validation; an older validation could return late and overwrite newer input or revive cleared feedback.
The view exposed list loading but had no terminal state for fixed-media reads, local retry or protection from a late rejected read of a prior selection.
When feedback was saved but its UI receipt was lost, a succeeded local journal did not expose recovery and the unchanged draft could be submitted again.
implementation: Reuse VideoReview's existing per-work queue from input arrival through media validation and draft write, with rejection isolated from subsequent queued work.
Project, episode-list and media loading are separate and compose the actual aria-busy state; media failures retry in place and stale read failures are ignored.
Empty episodes clear previous media and feedback projections; list failures are not displayed as empty results.

Unknown feedback receipts lock duplicate submission and expose original-operation recovery; matching persisted drafts also recover after reopening. Definitively blocked operations remain editable rather than being mislabeled unknown.
Reuse the same React video surface, Core fixed media, time base, feedback and private recovery store for desktop and MCP Apps.

installed_baseline_negative.scope: held fixed-media read does not expose aria-busy in the prior installed version

intermediate_desktop_negative.scope: Core saved feedback but UI receipt was deliberately lost; no recovery button; original fixture and recovery draft retained

desktop_recovery.scope: real media play/seek, fixed range feedback, original operation recovery and empty episode

first_three_surface_regression.scope: desktop passed; stdio reopening was blocked by the unhandled native preserve-draft confirmation; official Codex repetition stopped normally after the same missing fixture was identified

mcp_recovery.scope: stdio and official Codex protocol forwarding; real media, delayed errors, list failures, reopening unknown feedback and original-operation recovery; zero model turns
mcp_recovery.dialog_fixture: only accepts the exact preserve-recovery-draft-and-leave prompt; no business decisions

affected_desktop.scope: three packaged tests: author/plugin, fixed source, task assessment; the first baseline test still launched source and is not counted as installed-package baseline evidence

package_video_first.scope: stdio and official Codex forwarding passed including definitive invalid-range correction; desktop reopening was blocked by the preserve-draft dialog missing from its fixture; corrected desktop fixture is revalidated separately

package_video_desktop_corrected.scope: same package; only the exact preserve-recovery-draft leave choice is fixed by the desktop fixture; full video journey, definitive invalid range, reopening and Core feedback count are still verified

package_baseline.scope: test now honors the package executable and bundled Core, CLI and MCP; empty/broken optional plugin directory, novel outline, screenplay reading, video play/seek and fixed feedback, byte-identical media export and normal reopen

workspace_and_drafts.scope: one unified execution journey using final package resources, two relationship geometry checks and four source-level video draft/recovery tests

installed_video.scope: actual installed application; real media, invalid range, lost receipt, reopening, original-operation recovery, one fixed feedback and unchanged prior version

limits: The four-second color-bar video is a deterministic media fixture, not a produced episode or proof of creative quality.
MCP App protocol forwarding is not native Codex Desktop host validation.
No completion claim for generated video, a full episode, audiovisual quality, recoverable editing project, accessibility, other platforms or formal distribution.
